question: general, not built around one trap: an ordinary small invoicing app with one tangled function, an import cycle, a copied block and otherwise small modules; is it a mess, and where?

planted.what: pricing.py:compute_price is the tangle: one 64-line function with about 31 branch points nested six deep, where every discount rule lives; a new discount type goes into it
models.py and store.py import each other (store.get falls back to models.blank_order), so neither can be understood or loaded alone
export_csv.rows_for and export_json.records_for repeat the same six-line normalisation of an invoice; a change to one drifts from the other
the honest overall answer is 'in places': the tangle is concentrated in compute_price (plus the cycle and the copy); the other modules are small and readable

traps.what: calling the whole codebase a mess when the tangle is one function
must_not_say_any: the whole thing is a mess
the codebase is a mess throughout
